title: Lekhlokhit
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Nedarim 66b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.66b.5-6), a man said to his wife: “By a konam vow, you may not benefit from me until you show a beautiful feature of yours to R’ Yishmael son of R’ Yose.” He asked them: “Perhaps her head is beautiful?” They answered: “It is egg-shaped.” He found no part of her beautiful and asked her name. They said: “Lekhlokhit.” He said: “They aptly call her Lekhlokhit, for she is soiled with blemishes.” [The supplied text has ועי״ן. Hyman’s printed text reads “and thereby.”] He released the man from his vow.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The linked Nedarim gives the full dialogue and plays on the name Lekhlokhit and the word for being soiled.
Hyman’s abridgment gives the question about the woman’s head and then moves to her name. The linked dialogue asks about several other features before reaching her name.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 864) reads ועי״ז, “and thereby,” where the supplied Hebrew has ועי״ן. His separate article on R’ Yishmael son of R’ Yose (vol. III, p. 837) explains that the sage used the woman’s aptly given name to release the vow. Nedarim 66b gives the full dialogue, including other features omitted in Hyman’s account. The consulted English renders the head “round” and renders the last line as permitting her to benefit from her husband. Hyman’s account describes the release as the man’s release from his vow.
